title: A Protocol for the Vector
premise: Marguerite Dravenmoor, sole caretaker of Earth's abandoned seed vault, has spent fifteen years hauling cargo through contested orbits between the Meridian Compact and the Kessler Syndicate. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, he decodes it and discovers it was sent by his own hand — a message he will send forty years from now, warning of a war that annihilates both fleets. To prevent it, Marguerite fabricates evidence of a third, hidden fleet that neither side can afford to provoke, keeping the lie alive while smugglers, syndicate agents, and a Compact intelligence officer named Ilsa Vey close in on him. In the end, exposed and cornered, Marguerite chooses to broadcast the truth of his deception along with the seed vault's genetic archive — offering both fleets survival instead of victory — and the fragile peace that follows costs him his ship, his anonymity, and nearly his life, but buys the future the signal foretold.
about_author: Beatrix Pemberton is a former orbital logistics analyst who spent a decade writing technical manuals before turning to fiction. She lives in a converted lighthouse on the Atlantic coast, where she writes stories about people who keep things running when no one is watching.

chapters.title: The Quiet Orbit
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Fifteen years alone tending the seed vault, running cargo through contested space, his routines rendered in loving detail. The emotional beat is loneliness worn smooth into habit — until an anomalous signal pings his receiver in a language no one has spoken in two centuries.

chapters.title: Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. He decodes the signal using archived linguistic files and freezes: the syntax is his own idiosyncratic shorthand, dated forty years in the future. The beat is vertigo — the intimate horror of recognizing your own handwriting in a ghost's voice.

chapters.title: Cargo and Consequence
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A routine delivery to a Meridian Compact station goes wrong when Syndicate pirates board his hauler, and he barely escapes with the decoded signal intact. The beat is fear sharpening into resolve: the message mentions this exact skirmish, already written.

chapters.title: What the Signal Says
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Full translation: in forty years, both fleets destroy each other over the seed vault, and Earth's last biosphere burns with them. The emotional beat is grief for a future not yet lived, and the dawning weight of being its only witness.

chapters.title: Ilsa Vey
chapters.summary: Ilsa Vey's POV. A Compact intelligence officer notices Marguerite's flight path deviating toward restricted coordinates and opens a file on him. The beat is cold professional curiosity — she suspects smuggling, not prophecy, and her competence makes her dangerous.

chapters.title: A Fleet That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Desperate, he fabricates telemetry suggesting a hidden third fleet guards the vault, betting mutual fear will freeze both sides. The beat is transgressive exhilaration — the first lie of many, told to save everyone.

chapters.title: The Lie Takes Root
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Both fleets detect the phantom signatures; patrol patterns shift; stations go quiet with recalibration. The beat is dread disguised as success — the peace holds, but every hour the lie grows more elaborate and more brittle.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Debt
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Old friend and fence Dario Okafor demands payment for forged transponder data, forcing Marguerite into a risky run through Syndicate territory. The beat is the price of survival made literal: favors, debts, and bodies.

chapters.title: Interrogation at Meridian Gate
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She detains Marguerite under pretext of customs review and probes his story; he lies well but not perfectly. The beat is a duel of two careful minds, each sensing the other knows more than they say.

chapters.title: Ghost Signatures
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Cross-referencing sensor logs, she finds the phantom fleet's emissions match a decades-old decommissioned relay — someone manufactured the threat. The beat is the hunter's quiet thrill as the conspiracy acquires a human shape.

chapters.title: The Vault Below
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. He retreats to the seed vault itself, walking its frozen corridors of extinct crops, remembering why he stayed fifteen years. The beat is tenderness and resolve: this archive is the inheritance he refuses to let burn.

chapters.title: Dario's Price
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Syndicate enforcers capture Dario and torture his ledger loose; Marguerite learns his forgery trail leads straight to him. The beat is guilt curdling into panic — his lie will kill the man who helped him tell it.

chapters.title: Rescue at Kilometer Nine
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A brutal extraction attempt frees Dario but destroys half Marguerite's ship and exposes his route to both fleets. The beat is fury and grief — survival purchased with wreckage, and the clock now audibly ticking.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Trigger
chapters.summary: Fleet-commander POVs (Compact Admiral Sorel and Syndicate Broker Anselm). Each believes the other is massing for assault on the vault; each edges toward preemptive strike. The beat is tragic irony — the war Marguerite feared is assembling itself from his own fiction.

chapters.title: Vey Closes In
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She traces the forged telemetry to the seed vault and confronts Marguerite there, alone, unarmed. The beat is raw confrontation: she demands truth, and for the first time he gives it — the signal, the date, the extinction.

chapters.title: Believing the Impossible
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She verifies the signal's temporal impossibility against her own classified archives and finds corroborating anomalies. The beat is shattered certainty — a rational woman choosing to believe, because the alternative is worse.

chapters.title: Alliance of Liars
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Marguerite and Ilsa race to build a disclosure plan before either fleet strikes, knowing exposure of the lie could trigger the very war it prevented. The beat is wary trust becoming something like partnership, maybe more.

chapters.title: Anselm's Gambit
chapters.summary: Broker Anselm's POV. The Syndicate launches its preemptive strike early, having found Dario's second ledger. The beat is cold ambition meeting catastrophe — the timeline begins collapsing ahead of schedule.

chapters.title: Forty Years From Now
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Cornered in the vault as fleets converge, he realizes how the original signal must have been sent — by him, from this room, in the next hours. The beat is fatalistic clarity: the loop closes here, or breaks here.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax, shared POV. As weapons arm, Marguerite hijacks the vault's deep-space array and broadcasts everything: the lie, the truth, the signal, and the full genetic archive — survival offered freely to both fleets. The beat is sacrifice at maximum volume.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Truth
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Fleets stand down amid scandal; Sorel and Anselm face reckoning; Ilsa testifies to the impossible signal. The beat is exhausted, unglamorous peace — justice achieved entirely outside any law, at terrible cost.

chapters.title: Seeds
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, epilogue. Shipless and famous, he returns to the vault as its caretaker again, planting the first new growth from the archive. The beat is quiet hope: identity rebuilt, the future unwritten at last — except for one message he now knows he must someday send.
